question: Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das gave up their legal practices during which Movement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Non - Cooperation Movement.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:-**

 
 
• It was launched by **Mahatma Gandhi in 1920** as a response to the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre and the Rowlatt Act.
 
• The movement aimed to** boycott British goods, institutions, and courts **and to promote **Indian self-rule**.
 
• Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das were prominent leaders of the** Indian National Congress** who actively participated in the Non-Cooperation Movement.
 
• They gave up their** legal practices **as a symbolic gesture of their **commitment to the movement **and their rejection of British colonial rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Respect Movement:-**

 
 
• It was a **social reform movement **in South India led by **E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar)** in the 1920s and 1930s.
 
• It aimed to promote the **rights and dignity of non-Brahmin castes **and to challenge Brahmin hegemony.
 
 
 
• **Quit India Movement:-**
 
 
• It was a mass civil disobedience movement launched by **Mahatma Gandhi in 1942** demanding immediate** British withdrawal **from India.
 
 
 
• **Civil Disobedience Movement:-**
 
 
• It​ was a campaign of **nonviolent civil disobedience** led by Mahatma Gandhi in **1930 **to challenge British colonial rule and to demand Indian independence.
 
• It included the** Salt Satyagraha**, in which Indians defied British salt laws by making** their own salt.**
